nature-clim-128.q: What did Arab oil producers do in the 1973 oil crisis?
nature-clim-128.a: They embargoed shipments to Western Europe and the United States over their support for Israel.

nature-clim-123.q: What do system LCOE and similar metrics add to the cost of wind and solar power?
nature-clim-123.a: The cost of storage or backup plants needed when wind and solar are unavailable.

nature-clim-208.q: In terms like carbon-neutral economy, what does 'carbon' stand for?

nature-clim-153.q: How many people is fossil-fuel air pollution estimated to kill each year, as of 2019?

nature-clim-144.q: What share of the world's soil carbon do wetlands hold, and on how much of its land?
nature-clim-144.a: They hold 20-30% of it on only 5-8% of the world's land.

nature-clim-179.q: How much plant carbon stays in the soil under slash-and-burn compared with slash-and-char?
nature-clim-179.a: Slash-and-burn leaves only 3%, while slash-and-char can keep up to 50%.

nature-clim-177.q: What did Bohm (1993) first show about supply-side climate policy?
nature-clim-177.a: That taking fossil fuel reserves off the market can be a beneficial climate policy.

nature-clim-013.q: Why are climate services called demand-driven?
nature-clim-013.a: They are designed with users through co-design, rather than being supply-driven research products.

nature-clim-016.q: Why do resilience toolkits rely on long lists of proxy indicators?
nature-clim-016.a: Resilience has no single observable metric and includes intangibles like social capital.

nature-clim-035.q: Why is traditional indemnity insurance usually not viable for smallholders in developing countries?
nature-clim-035.a: Assessing their actual losses is too costly.

nature-clim-053.q: What is the ultimate aim of the UN climate convention, set out in Article 2?
nature-clim-053.a: To stabilise greenhouse gas concentrations at a level that prevents dangerous human interference with the climate system.

nature-clim-098.q: What were the pledges of the bottom-up climate approach renamed at Paris?

nature-clim-049.q: How much debt did Seychelles redirect to marine parks, ocean conservation and ecotourism in its debt-for-nature swap?

nature-clim-095.q: Why are HFCs a concern even though they do not harm the ozone layer?
nature-clim-095.a: They are greenhouse gases with a high global warming potential.

nature-clim-082.q: How have the wealthiest nations responded to climate reparations at the UNFCCC?
nature-clim-082.a: They have consistently opposed them, and before COP27 talks were steered to 'cooperation and facilitation' rather than liability.

nature-eecon-240.q: How do deductive, inductive and 'floating' models differ?
nature-eecon-240.a: A deductive model rests on theory, an inductive model on empirical generalization, and a floating model on neither.

nature-eecon-063.q: Why does Karl William Kapp call 'externalities' a misnomer for environmental harms?
nature-eecon-063.a: Because modern business makes profit by shifting costs onto others as normal practice.

nature-eecon-118.q: What do the first and second laws of thermodynamics say?
nature-eecon-118.a: The first says energy cannot be created or destroyed; the second says the total entropy of interacting systems never decreases.

nature-eecon-245.q: What share of global energy use and energy-related CO2 emissions do buildings account for as of 2020?
nature-eecon-245.a: 37%, or 39% when the manufacture of building materials is counted.

nature-eecon-127.q: Who contrasted a 'cowboy economy' with a 'spaceman economy' in a 1966 essay on Spaceship Earth?

nature-eecon-246.q: What is the foundation of post-Keynesian economics?
nature-eecon-246.a: The principle of effective demand: demand matters in the long run as well as the short run, so a market economy has no automatic tendency toward full employment.

nature-eecon-070.q: In ecological economics, whose writing on money can the work on debt, growth and money be traced to?

nature-eecon-120.q: How did nutrients sent to cities as food create a metabolic rift?
nature-eecon-120.a: They were not returned to the land as waste, a one-way 'robbing of the soil' that linked urban pollution with soil depletion.

nature-eecon-083.q: What did Gerard K. O'Neill plan in the 1970s, and why?
nature-eecon-083.a: Space settlements, to solve overpopulation and limits to growth without political repression.

nature-eecon-133.q: How large did Hickel and colleagues calculate the drain from the Global South to be for 1990 to 2015 under unequal exchange?
nature-eecon-133.a: Equivalent to 242 trillion in 2010 US dollars.

nature-eecon-247.q: Who developed the term urban metabolism in 1965, and what did he model?
nature-eecon-247.a: Abel Wolman, who modelled the inflows and outflows, mainly water and the waste it produces, of a hypothetical American city of 1 million people.

nature-eecon-104.q: What net energy gain does a process with an EROI of 5 yield?
nature-eecon-104.a: A net gain of 4 units for each unit spent.

nature-eecon-122.q: What does Moore hold about the split between social and natural systems?
nature-eecon-122.a: That it is empirically false and arbitrary.

nature-eecon-131.q: What advantage did Odum believe societies with access to higher-quality energy had?
nature-eecon-131.a: An advantage in the evolutionary struggle.

nature-eecon-212.q: Why is economic development controversial in debates on sustainable development?
nature-eecon-212.a: Because 'development' can be read as just economic growth, which can promote a system that is bad for the environment.

nature-eecon-226.q: Who introduced the two-factor capital-labour CES production function, and who popularised it?
nature-eecon-226.a: Solow introduced it; Arrow, Chenery, Minhas and Solow popularised it.
